turns.user: Can a landlord evict a tenant without giving any notice in India?
turns.answer:
No. A landlord cannot evict a tenant without first giving the notice prescribed by law.  

Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 provides that, in the absence of a written contract or contrary local usage, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed a year‑to‑year tenancy that may be terminated by either party only upon giving six months’ notice, and a lease for any other purpose is deemed a month‑to‑month tenancy that may be terminated only upon giving fifteen days’ notice. The notice must be in writing, signed by the person giving it, and must be sent by post or personally delivered (or affixed to the property if delivery is not practicable) [1].  

Thus, without serving the required written notice, a landlord has no legal right to evict the tenant.  

General background (not from the retrieved sources): The requirement of notice protects tenants from sudden loss of possession and ensures that any eviction process follows the procedural safeguards laid down in the relevant tenancy laws and court rules.
